subject: Banking
title: Wire Transfer Fees Explained
description: Learn Wire Transfer Fees Explained in one minute.

hook.text: Sending a domestic wire transfer costs $25-30. The actual processing cost to the bank is under $1.

buildup.text: Wire transfers move through the Fedwire system. The Federal Reserve charges banks $0.25 per wire.

discovery.text: International wires cost $40-50 and pass through correspondent banks. Each one takes a cut, adding layers of fees.

twist.text: Fintech apps like Wise charge 0.5-1% for international transfers. Banks charge 3-5% hidden in the exchange rate.

climax.text: Wire fees are legacy pricing. The cost is low, the markup is high, and only competition from fintech is changing it.

punchline.text: Costs the bank under $1. Costs you $25. Wire fees are pure markup.

quiz.question: What does the Federal Reserve charge banks per wire transfer?

details.summary: Banks charge $15 to $50 per wire transfer despite the actual processing cost being minimal. Wire fees are a profitable holdover from an era before instant digital payments, persisting because business customers have few alternatives for large transfers.
details.whyItMatters: Wire transfer fees represent banks monetizing their position as gatekeepers of the payment system. New payment technologies like real-time payments threaten this revenue stream by offering faster, cheaper alternatives.
takeaways: Domestic wire fees range from $15 to $30 and international wires cost $35 to $50
Actual processing costs are estimated at $1 or less per transaction
Real-time payment networks like FedNow are emerging as cheaper alternatives

faq.question: Why are wire transfers so expensive if the cost is minimal?
faq.answer: Wire fees are a legacy profit center. When wires were the only way to move large sums quickly, banks could charge premium prices. The fees persist because business customers need same-day settlement and alternatives have been slow to emerge.

faq.question: Will wire transfer fees eventually disappear?
faq.answer: Real-time payment networks like FedNow and The Clearing House's RTP offer instant transfers at much lower cost. As these networks gain adoption for business payments, wire transfer volume and fees are likely to decline significantly.
